MR BRAIN: 03/22/2023

HISTORY: Patient with recurrent Grade II oligoastrocytoma, initially
resected in 2005.

TECHNIQUE:

Sagittal T1 FFE, sagittal FLAIR, axial diffusion, axial 3-D T2,
axial perfusion, and 3-D T1 post-gadolinium.

IMPRESSION:

1. Evidence of a prior left parietal craniotomy with the
resection cavity affecting portions of the superior parietal
lobule. There is notable T2 prolongation in the surrounding
resection cavity with focal expansion of gyri, particularly
within the left superior parietal lobule. Additionally, T2
prolongation extends towards the posterior horn of the left
lateral ventricle with mild subependymal involvement. No distal
signal abnormality is present. These changes have progressed
since 2018.

2. No significant enhancement is observed. MR perfusion, despite
suboptimal quality, indicates increased blood volume within the lesion.

3. Collectively, these findings, along with increased mass effect,
increased blood volume, and prolonged T2 signal, raise concern
for recurrence of the previously resected oligoastrocytoma. There
is no indication of distal dissemination.

END OF IMPRESSION:

MR BRAIN WITH AND WITHOUT CONTRAST:  6/15/2024 3:45 PM
INDICATION (as provided by referring clinician): anaplastic oligoastrocytoma

Location: Left Temporal
Age at Diagnosis: 42 year old left-handed female
Treatment History:
1. Presented with headaches
2. 09/10/2015: Subtotal resection. Pathology: anaplastic oligoastrocytoma, 1p deleted and 19q intact
3. 09/10/2015: Completion of radiation plus temozolomide
4. Temozolomide x 12
5. 11/20/2017: Subtotal resection. Pathology: oligoastrocytoma WHO grade-3, 1p19q co-deleted
6. 12/15/2018: Completion of 12 cycles of temozolomide
7. 05/10/2024 - present: Ivosidenib 500mg daily
COMPARISON: MR of the Brain 4/20/2024
TECHNIQUE: Multiple sequences through the brain were acquired at 3.0 tesla.
MEDICATIONS:
Dotarem - 15 mL - Intravenous
FINDINGS:
Compared to 4/20/2024, stable appearance of infiltrative nonenhancing T2 FLAIR signal abnormality involving the right cerebellum, vermis, right and mid pons, right flocculus, and right superior and middle cerebellar peduncles which is nevertheless increased compared to more remote priors.
Unchanged postsurgical left temporal craniotomy and underlying resection cavity with moderate resection cavity and minimal associated peripheral blood products. No new or suspicious enhancement, T2/FLAIR signal, increased MRI perfusion, or reduced diffusion.
Similar patchy supratentorial white matter T2/FLAIR hyperintensities likely reflecting a combination of posttreatment changes and sequela of chronic microvascular ischemic disease.
Otherwise, no new intracranial hemorrhage, hydrocephalus, or mass effect. No acute infarct. No extra-axial collection. Unchanged ventricular configuration.

IMPRESSION: 
1. Compared to 4/20/2024, no definite evidence of disease progression. Similar appearance of diffuse nonenhancing infiltrative disease within the right posterior fossa involving the right cerebellum, right greater than left pons, and right superior and middle cerebellar peduncles.
2. No evidence of recurrent disease within the left temporal lobe.
